thread:
maya: quick design check — should required fields still use the red asterisk or switch to a subtle 'required' label? thinking about accessibility + screen reader clarity.
raj: i'm leaning toward explicit 'Required' text. a11y readers announce it better than an asterisk. also easier to translate.
e.loise: +1 for text. asterisk is ambiguous, users ask what it means all the time.
sam-dev: curious about visual density. adding 'Required' increases label width. can we use `aria-required` and hide text visually?
kate-ux: hiding text visually hurts discoverability. we should keep visible 'Required' for dense forms, maybe collapse on small screens.
maya: screenshots attached — compact vs relaxed spacing. compact keeps labels on one line, relaxed wraps 'Required' on a second line. which reads better?
raj: compact feels cluttered. relaxed looks clearer but costs vertical real estate. for onboarding flows we can trade space for clarity.
e.loise: can we try inline microcopy that only appears on focus? e.g., label showing 'Required' only when the field is focused or invalid.
sam-dev: that helps but adds motion complexity. also focus-only hints won't help keyboard users who tab past without expanding.
kate-ux: what about required badges on the form header instead? like a top legend: "Fields marked required", then keep asterisk small. tests show legend + asterisk still confuses screen readers.
maya: lighthouse-bot: accessibility scan: recommended visible label text for required fields.
lighthouse-bot: (automated) fails: form-aria-announce — missing visible required labels in 12 fields.
raj: ok, data-backed. let's prioritize visible "Required" text for fields where errors are common (email, password, billing info). others can use smaller indicators.
e.loise: moving to error presentation — inline errors vs toasts/top summary. Thoughts?
sam-dev: inline errors are faster to fix. top summary helpful for long forms when users miss multiple fields.
kate-ux: hybrid: inline for immediate feedback, plus a condensed top summary only on submit containing links to the invalid fields (anchor links).
maya: anchor links would be great for keyboard users. but we need to ensure focus management sends focus to first invalid field.
raj: implementation note: please avoid scroll-jacking — focus jump should be smooth and respects reduced-motion.
sam-dev: agree. i'll add `prefers-reduced-motion` checks. code stub: ```js
const el = document.querySelector('.first-error');
el.focus({preventScroll: false});
```
kate-ux: destructive actions confirmation — we have two flavors: modal typed-confirm vs simple undo toast. which do we prefer for 'delete project'?
e.loise: project deletion is destructive & irreversible for some customers. typed-confirm (enter project name) is safer.
raj: cost tradeoff: typed-confirm reduces accidental deletes but increases friction for power users. we could offer a setting to enable typed-confirm for orgs that opt-in.
maya: for free-tier flows, maybe simple modal with clear copy + red primary. for enterprise, require typed entry by default.
sam-dev: also add a server-side kill-switch: grace period soft-delete + data retention policy to allow recovery for a configurable window.
kate-ux: copy suggestion for modal header: "Delete project and all associated resources". body: "Type the project name to confirm. This action is permanent." CTA: "Delete project" (destructive, outline cancel).
e.loise: accessibility nit: ensure modal dialog has role="dialog" aria-modal="true" and the typed input is labelled programmatically. screen readers should announce how many characters required.
raj: large note — when showing inline validation for passwords, avoid real-time error messages that reveal password policy step-by-step for security. prefer generic hints and only validate at submit, or show policy without marking as failed until submit.
maya: great callout. keep security-sensitive feedback minimal.
e.loise: final ask: can design produce a compact and expanded spec (visual + copy + a11y notes) so eng can implement both variants?
sam-dev: i can take compact impl. raj can own expanded. we'll sync during next sprint.
maya: thanks everyone. i'll upload spec doc and a small prototype link. :sparkles:
